objective: Make the redaction applied to provider text before it becomes a row cover every credential this Brain issues, and apply it at the dispatch fire, which stores a provider's body without it. server/services/effects/failureDetail.ts `sanitizeProviderDetail` (~57) strips bearer tokens, key=value secrets, JWTs, signed-URL queries and `brnw_` worker credentials — but not the other three Brain-issued markers defined in server/services/identity/secrets.ts: `brnt_` (OAuth tokens, OAUTH_TOKEN_MARKER ~243), `brnv_` (invitations, INVITATION_MARKER ~252) and `brnc_` (bridge credentials, BRIDGE_CREDENTIAL_MARKER ~270). And `failureDetail` (~74) passes the error's own message through unmodified, so a credential inside the message half reaches `idempotency_attempts` untouched. Separately, server/services/dispatch/fire.ts stores `${response.status} ${detail.slice(0, 400)}` (~262-280) and a raw `error.message.slice(0, 400)` (~288-294) as the fire's message — which becomes `fleet_routines.state_reason` and bin events — with no redaction at all, relying on a comment's argument that the provider cannot echo the token. §17 and invariant 22 are unconditional: no credential in a log, an audit row, a response or an error. Neither module has a direct test (no file under tests/ imports failureDetail.ts or fire.ts's message path).
expectedOutcome: failureDetail.ts builds its marker patterns from the four markers imported (read-only) from server/services/identity/secrets.ts, so a marker added there is covered here without a second list; a separate exported `redactCredentials(text)` removes only credential-shaped substrings (every pattern in SECRETS) without collapsing whitespace or truncating, and `failureDetail` applies it to the message half as well, keeping the message otherwise byte-identical so every reader that matches on its words keeps working. fire.ts passes the provider body and the network error message through `sanitizeProviderDetail` before bounding, keeping the leading HTTP status and the existing 400-character bound, so a state reason such as `AUTH: 403 {"message":"routines are not available for this organization"…}` reads as it does today.
nonGoals: Editing anything under server/services/identity/**: the markers are imported, not changed.
Changing FireErrorKind classification, retry/backoff, quarantine rules or which rows the fire message is written to.
Changing the effects engine's control flow or what an attempt row records beyond redaction.
Redacting non-credential text: a message with no credential shape must be unchanged.
Any migration, schema or policy change.

acceptanceConditions.statement: sanitizeProviderDetail and redactCredentials remove a `brnw_`, `brnt_`, `brnc_` and `brnv_` credential of the shape each generator in server/services/identity/secrets.ts produces (generated in the test by calling those generators), leaving the surrounding words intact.

failureDetail(new Error('upload failed for brnc_<prefix>.<secret>')) contains neither the prefix-and-secret nor the secret, and failureDetail(new Error('The document store refused an upload (HTTP 400).')) with a detail carrying no secret returns the message byte-identical followed by the sanitized detail, as today.

A fire against a stubbed endpoint answering 403 with a body that echoes `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and a `brnt_` token returns a message that starts with `403`, contains neither token, and is at most 401 characters; a 403 body `{"message":"routines are not available for this organization"}` is preserved verbatim after the status.
The existing effects and dispatch suites (including tests/fleet.test.ts and any test asserting on a fire's AUTH state reason) still pass and the repository typechecks.

rollbackRequirement: Discard the branch. Wider redaction of provider text before it is stored; no schema, route, policy or control-flow change.
